verdict.rationale: Anytype has a first-party developer portal. It offers a versioned API reference and a published OpenAPI spec, says the API is meant to help developers "build powerful extensions," and includes an examples section (e.g., the MCP server). However, this is an external localhost API for integrations, not an in-app plugin system with a plugin SDK. API v2 is still pre-release, and only one sample is evidenced. Missing for 10: an in-app plugin/extension runtime and SDK, a broader set of documented sample plugins, independent hands-on corroboration of building extensions, and stable (non-pre-release) API status.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build my own plugins against a documented extension API/SDK with samples and developer docs

citations.quote: Learn how to query, retrieve, and update spaces, objects, properties, types, and templates to build powerful extensions.
Our API is now available and directly included with the desktop app, running entirely on localhost.
Anytype publishes a machine-readable OpenAPI document at developers.anytype.io/openapi-v2.yaml
Extensible through a gRPC API and AI "Agents" (see AGENTS.md).
The Anytype MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enabling AI assistants to seamlessly interact with Anytype's API through natural language.
